rationale: Verified field shapes against real captures before writing any parser code: search-payload fixtures for four sampled categories (electronics: search-payload.json/search-payload-custom-facets.json, clothing: search-payload-clothing.json, trading cards: search-payload-cards.json, toys: search-payload-toys.json) and item-detail HTML fixtures for the same categories (item-active-m71344610988.html electronics, item-active-m74693959349.html clothing, item-active-m14283608971.html toys, plus m80477245182/m89945662386) were inspected field-by-field with PowerShell JSON parsing (python3/node unavailable in this environment). This confirmed: search payload items carry a full itemCategoryHierarchy array (levels 0/1/2, id+name), inline brand/itemCondition/seller objects, and customFacetsList, but item-detail JSON has NO itemCategoryHierarchy array -- only a single itemCategory ref resolving to one leaf-level MasterItemCategory (id/name/level) via the __NEXT_DATA__ Apollo-style flat ref dictionary. Three fields were confirmed consistently absent/null across all 11 live samples rather than assumed present per the ticket's list: color is always null in the search payload, additionalAttributes is always empty/absent in item-detail JSON, and shippingPayer in the SEARCH payload is always {id:null,name:null,code:null} (only reliably available from the item-detail shippingPayer ref's code field). Implementation: MercariSearchPayloadParser.BuildSummary and MercariItemDetailJsonParser.BuildListing were extended with CategoryId/CategoryHierarchy/BrandId/ConditionId/SizeName/ColorName/ShippingPayer/SellerId/Attributes/RawJson (search) and the equivalent plus ShipsFromState/DiscountRatio/SellerProfile (item detail); MercariItemDetailSegmentationReader was extracted to hold the item-detail-specific ref-resolution logic (category hierarchy from a single leaf ref, seller profile from the seller ref including ratings/isProSeller/created-unix-seconds, additionalAttributes array reader) to keep MercariItemDetailJsonParser under the CI0014 200-line class-length limit. Persistence: ListingSegmentationUpserter.ApplyNew/ApplyEnrichment apply the same null-preserving merge pattern from #43 (core fields overwritten, enrichment fields null-coalesced against the existing stored value) so a rescrape that omits a field never erases what was previously stored; it was extracted from ListingUpserter for the same CI0014 reason. A new SellerEntity/Sellers table is upserted by SellerUpserter on every item-detail fetch (ItemDetailStore.ApplyItemDetail calls SellerUpserter.Apply after applying detail fields), keyed on the real non-zero Mercari seller id so no ValueGeneratedNever override was needed. Raw JSON is stored gzip-compressed in a new ListingRawData table (one row per listing, SearchItemJsonGzip/ItemDetailJsonGzip nullable BLOB columns, upserted independently so a search-only listing can later gain an item-detail blob without disturbing the search blob), exposed read-only via the new IListingRawDataStore/ListingRawDataStore (kept out of IScrapeStore/ScrapeStore to avoid tripping the CI0004 public-method-count limit, which ScrapeStore was already at). Average raw JSON size was measured by gzip-simulating the repo's GzipJson helper against the fixture corpus: search-item JSON averages ~1,244 bytes raw / ~552 bytes gzip; item-detail JSON averages ~2,463 bytes raw / ~921 bytes gzip; a fully-detailed listing (both blobs) averages ~3,707 bytes raw / ~1,473 bytes gzip, a ~60.3% reduction, confirming gzip is worthwhile. The EF migration (20260925024945_AddSegmentationSellersAndRawData) was generated with dotnet ef against the branch's actual current tip migration (20260924131942_AddBackfillItemPageFetches, unchanged on origin/main since branch creation) and hand-conformed to repo convention (internal partial class, // <auto-generated /> header, all /// XML doc comments stripped since NoCommentsAnalyzer blocks them at error severity); a dedicated test applies this migration on top of a database seeded only up to the pre-change migration and asserts the legacy row's Title/Price survive, new columns exist and are null on the legacy row, and no spurious Sellers/ListingRawData rows are created by the migration itself. No new fields are exposed through a new endpoint; ListingSummary (returned by the existing listings query path) carries all new properties. No extra network fetches were introduced -- all new logic reads fields already present in payloads the ETL already fetches (search payload, item-detail page), and this session did no live scraping, working entirely from already-captured fixtures. At base (before implementation) the command fails: none of ListingRawDataStore, ListingSegmentationUpserter, ListingSummaryMapper, MercariItemDetailSegmentationReader, SellerEntity/SellerUpserter exist, ListingSummary/ItemPageListing/ListingEntity lack the new properties, and the Listings table lacks the new columns, so every filtered test either fails to compile or fails to find the asserted data.
